defect: D12 (KEEP) / sanctioned oddity "groupId comes only from group-master prosecution cases"
title: groupId is emitted only when the prosecution case is a group master; applications never carry one

oracle.activityBoundary: every callActivity argument and return value crosses oracle/lib/boundary.js
oracle.determinismCheck: the case was run twice at clockPinIso and the two document arrays compared

edits: hearing: prosecutionCases[0].isGroupMaster deleted. prosecutionCases[0].groupId is deliberately LEFT IN PLACE — the whole point is that the value is available and still not used.

digests.convention: sha256 of the written file bytes — `sha256sum <file>` reproduces each value exactly

nodeEvidence.what: `getProsecutionCaseGroupId(prosecutionCase) { if (prosecutionCase.isGroupMaster) { return prosecutionCase.groupId; } }` — no else, so a non-master case yields undefined even when it HAS a groupId.
the only place groupId enters the identifier, and only for prosecution cases.
the court-application identifier literal has NO groupId key at all — an application-only authority can never have one.
first-occurrence-wins de-duplication by prosecutionAuthorityId: if a group-master case and a non-master case share an authority, whichever comes FIRST in the array decides whether groupId is present.
undefined groupId means the key is absent from the POSTed body (JSON.stringify drops undefined), not null.

assertion: The input is the group-master-case fixture with isGroupMaster deleted and the groupId field LEFT IN PLACE on the prosecution case. Assert EXACTLY: the single document has NO `groupId` key — assert key-absent, not null and not empty string. THE POSITIVE CONTROL: recorded/base__group-master-case is the identical fixture WITH isGroupMaster, and its document has groupId "47a08b62-e790-474b-94da-0fd406d2bcc8" (the same value asserted by the function app's own Jest test, SetInformantRegister/test/index.test.js:218). The pair pins the rule precisely: the groupId is present in the input in BOTH cases; only the isGroupMaster flag decides whether it reaches the wire. This is a KEEP (D12), not a bug: design_rules.md names it as intended behaviour — only masters carry the group. The trap it guards against is a Java port that reads groupId wherever it finds one, which would start populating group ids on ordinary cases and on applications. That would look like a tidy-up and would silently change what Results receives.
